review_notes: I read all 245 lines of the target file, plus the Mathlib sources it builds on: Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/DSlope.lean (definition of dslope, dslope_same, dslope_of_ne, dslope_sub_smul_of_ne, pow_sub_smul_iterate_dslope_of_zero, ContinuousLinearMap.dslope_comp), Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/AffineSpace/Slope.lean (slope_def_field, slope_def_module), Mathlib/Analysis/Analytic/IsolatedZeros.lean (has_fpower_series_dslope_fslope, has_fpower_series_iterate_dslope_fslope over general 𝕜,E), Mathlib/Analysis/Analytic/Basic.lean (AnalyticAt, HasFPowerSeriesAt), and Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Basic.lean (Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq). I also grepped the repository for uses of the reviewed declarations (PrincipalPart.lean, LaurentCoeff.lean), confirming all in-repo uses are over ℂ and analytic. Findings: (1) taylorCoeffAt_sub_pow_mul only uses differentiability at z₀, so AnalyticAt is unnecessary; (2) Filter.EventuallyEq.dslope_eq has no ℂ-specific content and generalizes verbatim to 𝕜 → E; (3) AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope likewise generalizes to 𝕜 → E using the existing general Mathlib lemma. I deliberately did not demand generalizing taylorCoeffAt itself to 𝕜 → E, since taylorCoeffAt_monomial (with `1 : E`) and taylorCoeffAt_const_mul are genuinely scalar-valued and the blueprint is over ℂ; I also did not claim that taylorCoeffAt_add/_sub can be weakened to DifferentiableAt, because the iterate induction needs differentiability of the iterated dslopes, which is currently supplied by analyticity. Proposed statements were not compiled (no execution available); in particular the weakened taylorCoeffAt_sub_pow_mul may need an explicit `DifferentiableAt.mul`/`DifferentiableAt.pow` term instead of relying on `fun_prop` with a merely differentiable hypothesis. Coverage is complete for the file; the remaining uncertainty is elaboration of the proposed variants.

findings.excerpt:
theorem taylorCoeffAt_sub_pow_mul (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀) (d j : ℕ) :
    taylorCoeffAt (fun z => (z - z₀) ^ d * g z) z₀ j
      = if j < d then 0 else taylorCoeffAt g z₀ (j - d) := by
findings.problem: The hypothesis `hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀` is much stronger than what the proof uses. The only place the hypothesis enters is the `d + 1`, `j + 1` case, where the proof needs `DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun z => (z - z₀) ^ d * g z) z₀`; the file itself records that this reduces to differentiability of `g` at z₀ (`have hg' : DifferentiableAt ℂ g z₀ := hg.differentiableAt`, line 183), and the `d = 0` case and the `j = 0` case use no hypothesis at all. The statement is therefore a purely differentiability-level identity artificially restricted to analytic functions.
findings.proposed_change:
Weaken the hypothesis to `(hg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g z₀)`:

  theorem taylorCoeffAt_sub_pow_mul (hg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g z₀) (d j : ℕ) :
      taylorCoeffAt (fun z => (z - z₀) ^ d * g z) z₀ j
        = if j < d then 0 else taylorCoeffAt g z₀ (j - d)

and in the `succ d`, `succ j` case discharge `hdiff` explicitly from `hg`, e.g. by `((differentiableAt_id.sub_const z₀).pow d).mul hg` (or keep `fun_prop` if it picks up the hypothesis). The two call sites in this file (lines 190 and 235) then pass `analyticAt_const.differentiableAt` and `(AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope hGan m).differentiableAt`.
findings.benefit: Users holding only a differentiability fact for `g` (e.g. from `ContDiffAt`, or a function defined only near `z₀`) can apply the monomial-shift workhorse, and the statement honestly reflects the mathematical content: the shift identity is a differentiability statement, not an analyticity one. Analytic call sites keep working after a one-token `.differentiableAt` insertion.

findings.excerpt:
theorem Filter.EventuallyEq.dslope_eq (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] g) :
    dslope f z₀ =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] dslope g z₀ := by
findings.problem: This lemma contains no complex analysis: `dslope`, `slope` and `Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq` are all stated in Mathlib over an arbitrary `NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜` and `NormedSpace 𝕜 E` (DSlope.lean line 30, `slope_def_module`). Restricting `f g : ℂ → ℂ` makes the result unusable for real-valued, p-adic-valued or vector-valued functions, even though the proof only unfolds `slope` and rewrites with the pointwise equalities; there is no ℂ-specific step. Grepping Mathlib confirms there is no `EventuallyEq` congruence lemma for `dslope` at any level, so this is a genuine gap being filled only in the scalar-complex case.
findings.proposed_change:
State it over a general field and normed space:

  theorem Filter.EventuallyEq.dslope_eq {𝕜 E : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
      [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {f g : 𝕜 → E} {z₀ : 𝕜}
      (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] g) : dslope f z₀ =ᶠ[𝓝 z₀] dslope g z₀

The proof is the current one, with the two `slope_def_field, slope_def_field` rewrites at line 71 replaced by `slope_def_module, slope_def_module` followed by `rw [hb, hz]` (the general slope is definitionally `(b - z₀)⁻¹ • (f b - f z₀)`, so the two hypotheses close the goal); the `b = z₀` case is unchanged, using `dslope_same` and `Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq`.
findings.benefit: The lemma becomes a field-generic congruence result that other developments (over ℝ, over vector-valued analytic functions) can reuse, matching the generality of the surrounding Mathlib `dslope` API, at no cost in proof length. Degenerate cases are unaffected: at `b = z₀` both sides are `deriv` values, which agree by `deriv_eq`, and for `b ≠ z₀` the scalar `(b - z₀)⁻¹` is multiplied by equal vectors.

findings.excerpt:
theorem AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀) (j : ℕ) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ ((Function.swap dslope z₀)^[j] g) z₀ := by
findings.problem: The proof is a two-line invocation of `HasFPowerSeriesAt.has_fpower_series_iterate_dslope_fslope`, which Mathlib proves for `f : 𝕜 → E` with `[NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]` (IsolatedZeros.lean lines 47-48 and 91-92). The statement of `AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope` mentions neither `taylorCoeffAt` nor any complex-specific operation, so pinning it to `ℂ → ℂ` and `AnalyticAt ℂ` is gratuitous and blocks use for real-analytic or vector-valued functions.
findings.proposed_change:
State it at the generality of the underlying Mathlib lemma:

  theorem AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope {𝕜 E : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
      [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {g : 𝕜 → E} {z₀ : 𝕜}
      (hg : AnalyticAt 𝕜 g z₀) (j : ℕ) :
      AnalyticAt 𝕜 ((Function.swap dslope z₀)^[j] g) z₀

The existing proof (`obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hg; exact ⟨_, hp.has_fpower_series_iterate_dslope_fslope j⟩`) is unchanged, and the in-file use at line 233 (`AnalyticAt.iterate_dslope hGan m`) still elaborates by unification at `𝕜 = E = ℂ`.
findings.benefit: The lemma becomes a reusable statement about the `dslope`-iterate of a general analytic function, complementing Mathlib's general analytic API (`AnalyticAt.eventually_eq_or_eventually_ne` etc.), and costs nothing but the type binders; no ℂ-specific content or degenerate case (including `j = 0`, where it is `hg` itself) is affected.
